title: GET /books serializes the whole list into a fixed 4096-byte buffer
evidence: http.c:174 `char *json = malloc(4096)`; the per-book strncat at http.c:199 is bounded, so a collection larger than ~4KB is silently truncated to invalid JSON rather than overflowing. Never triggers at the spec's test scale (<=3 books).
suggestion: Grow the buffer dynamically (realloc as books are appended) so large lists return valid JSON.

title: SQL built by string formatting instead of parameterized queries
evidence: db.c:155, db.c:252, db.c:310, db.c:328 build SQL via snprintf with manual single-quote doubling (db_get_books_by_author/db_create_book/db_update_book/db_delete_book). Single-quote doubling is correct SQLite escaping so no injection is demonstrable, but bind parameters are the safe idiom.
suggestion: Use sqlite3_prepare_v2 + sqlite3_bind_text/int for all writes and the author filter.

title: debug_db.c is dead code, not built or tested
evidence: Makefile:6 `SRCS = main.c http.c db.c` omits debug_db.c (148 lines); it is never compiled, linked, or exercised by run_tests.sh.
suggestion: Delete debug_db.c or fold it into an explicit debug build target.

title: create_book reuses the isbn buffer to parse the year field
evidence: http.c:313-315 extracts "year" into the `isbn` buffer, atoi's it, then re-extracts "isbn" over the same buffer. Functionally correct (isbn is overwritten last) but fragile; the agent's own log flagged this yet left it unchanged.
suggestion: Extract year into its own scratch buffer for clarity.

title: Repair agent stopped at the tool-call iteration limit without editing files
evidence: _agent_stdout.log:34 'Due to the tool call iteration limit, I'll provide the summary'; .hermes_usage.json shows completed:false, api_calls:90. The run still passes (test_coverage=1.0) because the prior attempt's code already worked — the earlier failure was environmental (cf. recent 'reap server processes / exp-43 port leak' fix), not a code defect the agent needed to fix.
suggestion: None — informational provenance for cross-run comparison of the repair stack.
